natalie (support): FYI escalation from AcmeHealth — they say a scheduled lab order tool got executed twice after a single generate call. Customer sees duplicate side-effect and double billing. ticket: INC-4632

aj (eng-runtime): ack. do we have the original request payload + any X-Request-Id / idempotency header?

anna (support): pasted the customer's raw payload below (redacted). They didn't set any idempotency header. They use our hosted API via SDK v2.

anna (support): ```json
{
  "model": "redwood-chat-1",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Place lab order for patient 123"}],
  "function_call": {"name":"create_lab_order","arguments": "{\"patient_id\":123,\"tests\":[\"CBC\"]}"}
```

chris (eng-sre): any logs for the request id? deploy-bot shows two downstream tool invocations at 2024-06-05T15:12:03Z and 2024-06-05T15:12:05Z for the same top-level request id.

deploy-bot: trace: r=tr_84d2a, tool-invoke create_lab_order id=tool_98ab timestamp=1719234723 result=200; tool-invoke create_lab_order id=tool_98ac timestamp=1719234725 result=200

aj (eng-runtime): that pattern (two tool invocations separated by ~2s) looks like our runtime retried the tool-call because it detected a transient network error when receiving the tool's callback, while the tool actually succeeded on the first attempt. The runtime then proceeded to deliver a success path and also retried the call, which the customer's tool executed again.

natalie (support): customer says their webhook returned 200 immediately and their logs show first call had full order details; second call is identical. They are charged for two side-effects.

aj (eng-runtime): two root causes we need to consider: 1) client SDK retried the top-level generate (leading to duplicate model requests -> duplicate tool calls), 2) runtime retries the tool invocation when it doesn't get an acknowledgement. We should check both. Do we have SDK/client request logs?

anna (support): customer confirmed no client retry — single request from their app. They use SDK v2 default settings. I grabbed the request headers they forwarded: `Authorization: Bearer <redacted>`, no `Idempotency-Key`, `X-Request-ID: r_84d2a`.

chris (eng-sre): ok runtime traces show single root incoming request r_84d2a. So client retry unlikely. Runtime trace: attempt 1 -> sent tool invoke to https://acmehealth.internal/hooks/labs (POST) -> got 200 but callback ack to runtime timed out due to a transient conn reset on our side. Runtime marked it as "no ack" and scheduled a retry. Second attempt succeeded fully.

aj (eng-runtime): this is a known gap: our outgoing tool invoker waits for a synchronous ack handshake (200 + body with {ack:true}) by default. If the ack path is interrupted but the downstream already processed, we risk duplicate exec on retry. We currently have no dedupe layer for tool adaptors.

natalie (support): customer asks immediate mitigation — how to avoid duplicates while we patch?

aj (eng-runtime): short-term: we can disable automatic internal retries for that customer (per-tenant runtime policy) so the second attempt won't be sent. I'll roll a safe config change to set tool_invoke_retry=0 for customer AcmeHealth. That will prevent retries but won't undo the duplicate that already happened.

chris (eng-sre): also recommend refunding the duplicate side-effect billing. Support can issue a credit for the duplicate execution and mark bill as dispute.

anna (support): doing that after we confirm which invocation IDs correspond to billed units. Can you provide tool execution ids?

deploy-bot: tool exec ids: ["tool_98ab","tool_98ac"], billed token units: 134 and 2 external action fees.

aj (eng-runtime): longer-term fix options: 1) require/endorse an `Idempotency-Key` header on generate when tool-calls are possible and have runtime dedupe keyed by (customer, idempotency-key, function_name), 2) add server-side dedupe token we return to tool adaptors so adaptors can return 409 for duplicate tool invocation attempts, or 3) change handshake to be more robust (ack with explicit tool-invoke-id in body) and improve network reliability.

chris (eng-sre): I think (1) + (2) is best: customers can opt-in immediately by setting Idempotency-Key; we can add runtime support without risky changes to handshake semantics. We should also add a one-time server-side cache for recent tool-invoke request hashes to dedupe duplicates within a short window.

natalie (support): customer can't deploy changes quickly. They asked for a quick flag to turn off retries and for a recommended webhook-level idempotency check on their side.

aj (eng-runtime): immediate actions I will take: 
- flip runtime config for AcmeHealth: tool_invoke_retry -> 0 (will push in 10m)
- add an incident note + runbook for support: how to map tool_exec_ids -> billing and issue credit
- open a PR for short-term server-side dedupe cache (ttl=30s) keyed on digest(request_body + function_name + customer_id)

aj (eng-runtime): repro steps for engineers: 
1) curl our generate endpoint with payload above (no idempotency key).
2) Simulate transient conn reset between runtime and tool by dropping the handshake packet after tool processes request. We have a test harness in eng-runtime/ci that can simulate this.

aj (eng-runtime): example curl: 
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '@payload.json'
```

anna (support): will coordinate with AcmeHealth on the disable-retry toggle and follow up with billing credit.

chris (eng-sre): I'll schedule a short postmortem with eng-runtime to decide whether the dedupe cache is safe and what SLA impact might be. Add owners: aj (eng-runtime) and chris (eng-sre).

natalie (support): thanks all. Customer expects update within 24h. I'll post status. :thumbsup:

anna (support): customer confirmed they see only one new invocation after we flip the flag in ~15m. They asked support to confirm billing credit after the flip.
